name: API versioning plan
needs: change my API without breaking customers' code
should I put v1 in the URL
rename a field in a public API
old mobile app versions still call the API
summary: A written rule for how your API changes over time: what counts as breaking, how a new version is chosen by callers, and how long old versions keep working. Adding fields is usually safe. Removing or renaming them is not.
need_when: Anyone outside your own frontend calls your API, including your own mobile app that users don't update.
skip_when: The API is only used by a web frontend you deploy at the same time.

ways.title: Version in the URL
ways.how: /v1/orders and later /v2/orders. Old routes keep working until a published sunset date.
ways.tradeoff: Obvious and easy to cache. Big jumps tend to bundle many changes at once.

ways.title: Dated versions per account
ways.how: Each account is pinned to the version it started on and can send a version header to upgrade. Small transform layers translate old shapes.
ways.tradeoff: Smooth for customers, and it is the model Stripe documents. More code to keep each old shape alive.

ways.title: Additive changes only
ways.how: Never remove or rename. Add new fields and endpoints, mark old ones deprecated in docs and responses.
ways.tradeoff: No version math. The API slowly collects leftovers.

prompt:
Write and apply an API versioning plan for my API.

Requirements:
- List what counts as a breaking change (removing or renaming a field or endpoint, changing a type, new required input, changed error codes) and what doesn't (new optional fields, new endpoints).
- Use [URL versions like /v1/] and route all current endpoints under v1.
- Add Deprecation and Sunset headers to anything scheduled for removal, plus a changelog page.
- Keep contract tests that pin the v1 response shapes so an accidental break fails CI.
- Log which version each API key or app build uses, so I know who still calls old versions.
- Document the policy: how much notice before removal ([6 months]) and how customers are told.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Renaming a field in a v1 response makes a contract test fail.
2. Deprecated endpoints return Deprecation and Sunset headers.
3. A dashboard or query shows request counts per version.
4. The changelog lists every breaking change with a date.
5. An old mobile build can still log in and load data.
acceptance_checks: Renaming a field in a v1 response makes a contract test fail.
Deprecated endpoints return Deprecation and Sunset headers.
A dashboard or query shows request counts per version.
The changelog lists every breaking change with a date.
An old mobile build can still log in and load data.
if_you_skip_it: One deploy breaks every customer integration and older app installs at once, with no warning.
